articles.title: GoPro’s Next Opportunity Could Lie Beyond the Action-Camera Market
articles.content: GoPro’s Next Opportunity Could Lie Beyond the Action-Camera Market Vardah Gill Wed, September 2, 2026 at 9:37 PM EDT 3 min read GPRO 688775.SS GoPro, Inc. (NASDAQ: GPRO ) is being acquired by Starman Optical in a $285 million all-cash deal, with Starman taking a 90% stake while existing GoPro shareholders retain 10%. The transaction values GoPro at $1.14 per share, representing about a 29.5% premium to the stock's previous closing price. The deal comes as GoPro faces significant challenges, including declining revenue, strong competition from DJI and Insta360, and higher memory-chip costs. GoPro has also warned about substantial doubt over its ability to continue as a going concern. GoPro’s Next Opportunity Could Lie Beyond the Action-Camera Market Bull Case The strongest argument for GoPro, Inc. (NASDAQ:GPRO) is the financial relief provided by the transaction. Starman's acquisition is expected to repay GoPro's debt, potentially removing one of the company's biggest near-term pressures. A stronger balance sheet could allow GoPro to focus on product development and finding new revenue opportunities rather than managing financial constraints. The deal could also help GoPro, Inc. (NASDAQ:GPRO) move beyond the increasingly competitive action-camera market. GoPro owns more than 2,500 U.S. patents, including technology involving optics and imaging. Starman, meanwhile, has expertise in optical transceivers used in AI data centers. Combining these capabilities could create opportunities in areas such as AI infrastructure, commercial imaging and defense. This could be particularly valuable as demand for optical connectivity continues to rise alongside AI data-center expansion. If Starman can successfully apply GoPro's intellectual property to these higher-growth markets, the acquisition could ultimately unlock value that GoPro was unable to realize as an independent consumer-electronics company. Bear Case The transaction also underscores the severity of GoPro, Inc. (NASDAQ:GPRO)'s underlying problems. The company's revenue has fallen sharply from its 2014 peak, while competition from Chinese manufacturers has put additional pressure on its core camera business. This raises questions about whether the GoPro brand can regain meaningful growth even with Starman's financial backing. Another concern is execution risk. Starman's optical-transceiver business and GoPro's consumer-camera operations are very different, and it could take significant time and investment to turn GoPro's patents and imaging expertise into commercially successful products outside its traditional market. Shareholders also give up most of their ownership in the transaction. With existing investors retaining just 10%, they will have limited participation in any future upside created by GoPro's technology. The fact that the stock traded above the $1.14 offer price could also indicate that some investors believe the company's assets may ultimately be worth more than the current deal implies. Story Continues Conclusion Overall, the deal is more positive for GoPro, Inc. (NASDAQ:GPRO)'s survival and long-term strategic potential than for its existing consumer business. Starman can provide financial stability and potentially put GoPro's technology into faster-growing markets such as AI infrastructure and defense. However, the weak camera business, competitive pressures, and uncertainty around monetizing its intellectual property remain significant risks. The transaction gives GoPro a fresh opportunity, but Starman will need to execute well for that opportunity to translate into meaningful long-term value. While we acknowledge the potential of GPRO as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: A Bigger Geothermal Bet: What Google’s Fervo Deal Could Mean
articles.content: A Bigger Geothermal Bet: What Google’s Fervo Deal Could Mean Vardah Gill Wed, September 2, 2026 at 9:39 PM EDT 5 min read FRVO GOOG SHEL Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ: FRVO ) has signed its largest-ever geothermal power agreement with Google, under which it will supply nearly 400 megawatts of electricity from its Cape Station project in southwestern Utah starting in 2028. The project is expected to become the world's largest enhanced geothermal facility, with Fervo investing more than $2 billion in its development. Google also has an option to purchase an additional 600 MW, potentially bringing the total arrangement close to 1 GW by 2030. The agreement is important because it gives Fervo a major technology customer at a time when AI data centers are creating strong demand for reliable, around-the-clock electricity. Fervo already has roughly 1 GW of power under contract, including agreements with Google, Shell, and Southern California Edison. A Bigger Geothermal Bet: What Google’s Fervo Deal Could Mean A Potential Breakthrough for Fervo The biggest positive for Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ:FRVO) is that Google is not just an investor or early-stage partner. It is becoming a significant customer. The companies began working together through Fervo's 3-MW Nevada pilot, followed by a 115-MW agreement involving Google and NV Energy. The new agreement represents a substantial increase in scale and suggests Google has gained confidence in Fervo's geothermal technology. That could make it easier for Fervo to attract additional large customers looking for dependable clean power. Data centers need electricity around the clock, making geothermal particularly attractive compared with intermittent sources such as solar and wind. Grid connection delays are also making it increasingly difficult for data-center operators to secure new power capacity quickly. Fervo could benefit if hyperscalers increasingly view geothermal as part of their long-term energy strategy. The potential additional 600 MW from Google is particularly significant. If exercised, it would give Fervo a much larger contracted pipeline and could strengthen the company's position as a major supplier of clean baseload power. Fervo's model uses drilling and hydraulic-fracturing techniques adapted from the oil and gas industry to create geothermal reservoirs. The Cape Station project represents a major test of whether that approach can be deployed economically at commercial scale. The company raised more than $2 billion in its May IPO, giving it substantial capital to accelerate project development. Management's ability to convert that capital into contracted projects could support rapid revenue growth over the coming years. Story Continues The long-term opportunity is potentially much bigger than the Google contract itself. If Fervo demonstrates that enhanced geothermal can reliably produce large amounts of electricity at competitive costs, the technology could be deployed across additional locations. That would allow Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ:FRVO) to build a broader portfolio of geothermal projects rather than relying on a handful of customers. The Google relationship could also serve as a reference point when negotiating with other technology companies and utilities. What Could Disrupt the Growth Story The biggest risk is execution. The Google agreement does not eliminate the risks involved in building Cape Station. The project is expected to require more than $2 billion of investment, and Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ:FRVO) still needs to demonstrate that enhanced geothermal can operate reliably and economically at this scale. A delay in drilling, construction, grid connection, or commissioning could push back revenue and increase capital requirements. Since Cape Station is considerably larger than Fervo's earlier projects, investors should not assume that the company's pilot success automatically translates into commercial-scale economics. Google's planned Utah data-center presence is not completely finalized. The company still needs to work through local and state approvals, while the data-center location itself has yet to be determined. This creates a potential timing mismatch. Fervo could have the generation capacity available while the associated data-center demand or infrastructure takes longer to materialize. Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ:FRVO)'s growth strategy requires substantial upfront spending. The company has raised significant capital, but developing large geothermal facilities requires continued investment before projects begin generating meaningful cash flow. If drilling or construction costs rise, the economics of future projects could become less attractive. Investors therefore need to focus not just on the number of megawatts under contract, but also on the cost of producing each megawatt and the returns generated on the capital invested. The broader bullish thesis depends on Fervo proving that enhanced geothermal can be replicated economically. The company has demonstrated the technology at smaller scales, but Cape Station is intended to be the world's largest enhanced geothermal project. That creates a meaningful technology and operational risk. If reservoir performance, drilling productivity, or operating costs fall short of expectations, Fervo's expansion plans could become more difficult and expensive. Conclusion The Google agreement is a strong strategic positive for Fervo Energy Company (NASDAQ:FRVO), because it provides commercial validation, a large anchor customer, and exposure to the rapidly growing electricity needs of AI data centers. The potential 600-MW expansion also gives Fervo meaningful upside if Cape Station performs as planned. The key question, though, is whether Fervo can turn contracted demand into profitable, large-scale geothermal generation. The company now has the capital and customer demand to pursue rapid expansion, but Cape Station's execution will determine whether Fervo can establish enhanced geothermal as a commercially viable industry. Overall, the news strengthens the long-term bull case, but Fervo remains an execution-heavy growth story. Success at Cape Station could significantly improve its growth prospects, while delays, cost overruns, or weaker-than-expected geothermal performance could quickly challenge the investment thesis. While we acknowledge the potential of FRVO as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses
articles.content: Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on x (opens in a new window) Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on facebook (opens in a new window) Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on linkedin (opens in a new window) Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on whatsapp (opens in a new window) Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on x (opens in a new window) Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on facebook (opens in a new window) Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on linkedin (opens in a new window) Chicago: the ultimate insider addresses on whatsapp (opens in a new window) Hannah Edgar Published September 4 2026 Jump to comments section Print this page Unlock the Editor’s Digest for free Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter. This article is part of FT Globetrotter’s guide to Chicago When I say Chicago isn’t a celebrity town, that cuts both ways. We have limited tolerance for Instagram culture, we roll our eyes at round-the-block queues and, for most of us, the very notion of $20 trend smoothies triggers an allergic reaction. On the other hand, we can be provincial. At a recent concert at the Jay Pritzker Pavilion in Millennium Park, the Jumbotron cycled through drone footage of American skylines. At the sight of Chicago’s, the crowd exploded. At all others, including a glimmering and handsome New York City? Crickets. Chicagoans have a funny relationship to fame. Seeing a celebrity out and about is not just another Tuesday for us: it’s day-derailing. We’ll ignore the cardinal rule imparted by our peers on the coast and bug the hell out of them, then spend the rest of the day calling our cousins’ cousins. We keep our local celebrities close but feel inordinately stung when they decamp for another city. To better understand this hot-and-cold city, we spoke to eight cultural insiders who know it better than most. Some were forged in Chicago. Others enthusiastically adopted it. And many of them still choose to live here, even when New York and LA beckon. Jump straight to . . . Writer Sandra Cisneros / Wilco frontman Jeff Tweedy / Chef-restaurateur Rick Bayless / Author and scholar Eve L Ewing / Lyric Opera of Chicago conductor and music director Enrique Mazzola / Saxophonist and composer Isaiah Collier / Chef-restaurateur Grant Achatz / Singer-songwriter and poet Tasha Sandra Cisneros, writer and author of ‘The House on Mango Street’ (born and raised in Chicago; based in San Miguel de Allende, Mexico) Where she’d take someone who already thinks they know Chicago The Aon Center . After going to a concert downtown in Grant Park, we would walk over to what was the Standard Oil Building, now the Aon Center, on East Randolph Street. In the plaza’s sunken garden is the most fabulous treasure: wind sculptures by Harry Bertoia . They look like reeds, and at the dedication ceremony in 1972, the artist climbed inside the installation and “played” them. ‘Untitled Sounding Sculpture’ by Harry Bertoia in the plaza of the Aon Center, which was redesigned by HGA © Andrew Bruah Bertoia was a furniture designer, too. When his sculptures were displayed at the Art Institute of Chicago in 1975, it was the first and only time I’d seen a sign that said, “Please touch.” I like the idea that he thought about the poetics of these sculptures moving and making these wonderful sounds. Something about Chicago that only other Chicagoans seem to understand Hot dogs . If you haven’t had a Chicago hot dog, you haven’t had a hot dog. You have to have a bun with little poppy seeds on it, it has to be bundled in waxed paper and the french fries have to be good. Now, there are even vegan hot dogs. Recently, my family and I got some at Portillo’s late at night, and they were really good — I was surprised! Cisneros rates the vegan hot dogs at Portillo’s . . . © Felix Choo/Alamy . . . which she recently tried late one night © Christopher Dilts/Bloomberg One more thing I didn’t realise until two years ago that the flowers in Chicago’s public parks were so much a part of the city. To me, lilacs, peonies and lilies of the valley are the quintessential flowers of Chicago. Jeff Tweedy, musician and lead vocalist/guitarist of Wilco (based in Chicago) Where he’d take someone who already thinks they know Chicago The parks . If you want to soak up what the city and culture are really like, I’d pick any of the Chicago Park District parks, like Independence in Irving Park or Gompers in North Park. Have a picnic and see how Chicagoans really recreate. Something about Chicago that only other Chicagoans seem to understand “Dibs” . The concept of saving your parking spot, especially in heavy snow. Technically not legal, but ultimately, pretty fair and moral. If you’re the one who broke your ass shovelling snow, you should get to keep that spot for at least a day or so. Tweedy says Chicagoans have an innate understanding of ‘dibs’ — the concept of saving your parking spot, especially in heavy snow’ © Getty Images What Chicago teaches you When you grow up in a smaller town like I did, there’s a belief that it’s a kinder way to live and that you can’t get that in a city. It’s not true. When I moved to Chicago, I knew more people in my neighbourhood than I did growing up — it’s all about block parties and meeting up with neighbours. Chicago has problems like everywhere else, but it’s a city that facilitates community. Rick Bayless, chef and restaurateur (based in Chicago) Where he’d take someone who already thinks they know Chicago The National Museum of Mexican Art . Rather than establishing the museum downtown, the founders chose Pilsen — a predominantly Latino neighbourhood — and they chose to keep this world-class collection free to all. NMMA is not only one of our city’s best museums but an integral player in this vibrant community. The National Museum of Mexican Modern Art, in Chicago’s Pilsen neighbourhood © Courtesy of NMMA ‘El Columpio’ (The Swing), 1990, by Alejandro Nava, is among the works in the museum’s collection © Courtesy of the artist and NMMA Something about Chicago that only other Chicagoans seem to understand Storefront theatre . Yes, we have grand old theatres that host Broadway touring companies, and yes, we have the internationally acclaimed Steppenwolf, Goodman and Chicago Shakespeare companies. But Chicago is a city of neighbourhoods, and most of them are home to a host of storefront theatres. One of the best is TimeLine Theatre Company, which does historical pieces that have contemporary relevance. Hungry yet? Forty years ago, when we opened Frontera Grill , farmers’ markets hadn’t taken off in Chicago. Today, with local chefs championing local products, there are over 40 and growing. Now communities are hosting “alternative” farmers’ markets that start at 3pm or 4pm and sell until around 7pm on specific weekdays, rather than weekend mornings. Eve L Ewing, author, scholar and co-owner of Build Coffee & Books in Woodlawn (based in Chicago) Where she’d take someone who already thinks they know Chicago The South Shore Nature Sanctuary and Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary . Our city motto is urbs in horto — city in a garden. Away from all the noise and the hubbub, the marshlands and prairie are also part of our identity. South Shore Nature Sanctuary, one of the green spaces that are also part of Chicago’s identity © Eric Alix Rogers Something about Chicago that only other Chicagoans seem to understand Community . The city is famously corrupt, but there’s a more generous way to understand the “you scratch my back and I’ll scratch yours” way we do things, which is that Chicagoans look out for each other and take care of one another. If you’re my neighbour’s cousin’s pick-up basketball buddy, you’re in the circle and I’ve got to take care of you. articles.title: Zcash Hits Highest Price in Nearly a Decade, Crushing Short Bets
articles.content: Zcash Hits Highest Price in Nearly a Decade, Crushing Short Bets Jose Antonio Lanz Fri, September 4, 2026 at 12:24 PM EDT 3 min read ZEC-USD DOGE-USD Zcash broke above $1,000 on Friday, its best price in almost a decade, extending a run that started near $500 a month ago. The token touched an intraday high of $1,029 on Binance before easing to around $984, up roughly 20% over 24 hours, scoring a new all-time high. The privacy coin's market cap climbed toward $17 billion, enough to push ZEC past Dogecoin among the ten largest cryptocurrencies, according to CoinMarketCap. Myriad: Where does XRP price go next? Click to make your prediction . The break above $1,000 caught short sellers off guard. About $34.5 million in short bets got force-closed as the price of Zcash punched through the round number, according to CoinGlass data, pushing total ZEC liquidations to roughly $36.6 million. Every trader forced to buy back a short adds real demand, which is part of why the rally kept accelerating. A squeeze years in the making Zcash is a so-called privacy coin, one of several in crypto but arguably the best known alongside Monero, which trades as XMR. It launched in 2016, created by cryptographer Zooko Wilcox and a team of researchers. Unlike Bitcoin and Ethereum, where transactions are visible on a public ledger by default, Zcash is designed to keep them private, using zero-knowledge cryptography to conceal who sent what to whom—and how much—while still proving that the transaction is valid. The coin is currently on one of the most impressive runs in the crypto market, especially among older digital assets. It has gained about 94% over the past 30 days and more than 2,300% over the past year, outpacing every other large-cap crypto asset even after an eight-year high in August. Grayscale's Zcash ETF began trading on NYSE Arca under the ticker ZCSH on August 25, giving brokerage investors a way into ZEC without a wallet. The daily chart shows why some traders are cautious even as the trend stays intact. The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, sits at 78.6, well past the 70 level traders read as overbought, while the 50-day moving average sits above the 200-day in a bullish setup. It means short-term demand is outpacing long-term, which bodes well for new buyers. Zcash (ZEC) price data. Image: Tradingview The Average Directional Index, or ADX, which tracks trend strength regardless of direction is currently at 48, well above the 25 mark traders use to determine a real trend is in place. And with positive momentum outpacing negative, it points to a trend still forceful enough to keep pushing through overbought conditions, at least for now. While Zcash is in price discovery mode, the $892.94 and $808.63 retracement levels are the logical support if the rally cools. Story Continues Zcash is also outrunning Bitcoin, but they started the week on the same trigger. Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000 Thursday after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's remarks pulled September hike odds lower and set off more than $415 million in short liquidations across the broader market. That reversed Friday morning. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported the U.S. economy added 162,000 jobs in August, well above the 56,000 consensus estimate, with unemployment holding at 4.1%. Bitcoin fell back below $80,000 as traders priced in better odds of a hike at the Fed's September 15-16 meeting, with next Friday's August CPI report now the number to watch. articles.title: MIMRYLO Approval Triggered $275M Payments for Protagonist (PTGX). Are Royalties the Better Commercial Model?
articles.content: MIMRYLO Approval Triggered $275M Payments for Protagonist (PTGX). Are Royalties the Better Commercial Model? Jeff Lewis Fri, September 4, 2026 at 12:14 PM EDT 4 min read PTGX TAK U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of MIMRYLO, or rusfertide, for erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera triggered $275 million in payments to Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: PTGX ). The amount consists of an additional $200 million opt-out fee and a separate $75 million approval milestone. Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) chose royalties over the original 50:50 U.S. profit-and-loss arrangement with Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited (NYSE:TAK). The April 2026 opt-out established tiered royalties of 14% to 29% on worldwide net sales and left Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) eligible for up to $875 million of additional milestones. The structure trades commercial control and uncapped profit participation for approval-triggered, non-dilutive capital, lower execution risk, and a high royalty share. Is Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (PTGX) the Best Cancer Stock to Invest in for Long-Term Gain? Bull Case The approval made another $275 million payable, in addition to the $849.5 million of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities reported by Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) as of June 30. The June balance already included the initial $200 million opt-out payment received during the second quarter. The royalty structure is unusually favorable for a fully partnered medicine. The approximate 21% weighted-average rate disclosed by Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) mechanically implies about $315 million of gross annual royalties at $1.5 billion of annual net sales, before contractual reductions and the separate obligation of Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) to pay a third party a 1% royalty on worldwide rusfertide net sales. The top 29% tier applies to incremental annual net sales above $1.5 billion. Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited (NYSE:TAK) holds exclusive worldwide development and commercialization rights and assumes the principal operating and financial responsibility. Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) can therefore direct capital toward wholly owned programs without funding a commercial organization for MIMRYLO. In the 293-patient Phase 3 VERIFY trial, 76.9% of patients receiving MIMRYLO plus current standard of care achieved the primary response endpoint during weeks 20 through 32, compared with 32.9% receiving placebo plus current standard of care. The endpoint measured the absence of phlebotomy eligibility. MIMRYLO also improved hematocrit control, phlebotomy burden, and fatigue measures. Bear Case Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) no longer controls pricing, market access, launch sequencing, or commercial investment. Those decisions depend on execution by Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited (NYSE:TAK). The 50:50 arrangement might have produced greater long-term economics if MIMRYLO becomes a major product, although Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) would also have absorbed half of U.S. operating losses and commercialization costs. Story Continues The $875 million of potential additional milestones is contingent. International regulatory approvals, sales thresholds, and commercial execution must occur before much of that value becomes cash. Royalty payments may also be reduced under specified contractual circumstances. MIMRYLO is a once-weekly subcutaneous treatment entering a market that includes phlebotomy and established cytoreductive therapies. The most common adverse reactions were injection-site reactions and anemia, and the label includes a warning for new or worsening thrombocytosis. Payer access and physician adoption will determine whether the headline royalty rates produce meaningful revenue. Hedge Fund Sentiment The filings available so far reflect positions held before Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) reported FDA approval of MIMRYLO. Insider Monkey's database showed 43 hedge funds holding Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX) at the end of 2Q2026, up from 42 funds three months earlier. Conclusion Partnering appears to be the better risk-adjusted commercial model for Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:PTGX). The structure provides immediate non-dilutive capital, preserves substantial worldwide participation, and transfers most launch costs and execution risk to Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited (NYSE:TAK). Whether it proves economically superior to the abandoned profit share remains unresolved. MIMRYLO must achieve broad access and durable adoption before the 14% to 29% royalties become a recurring cash-flow engine. While we acknowledge the potential of PTGX as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: Diesel prices hit an all-time high, pressuring economy ahead of midterms
articles.content: Diesel prices hit an all-time high, pressuring economy ahead of midterms Jake Conley · Breaking Business News Reporter Fri, September 4, 2026 at 12:01 PM EDT 3 min read US diesel prices raced up to an all-time high on Friday, crossing into new heights as wars in Iran and Russia-Ukraine keep structural pressure on an already tight market for the world's "workhouse fuel." Prices on Friday climbed to $5.85 per gallon in the retail diesel market, per data from AAA , well surpassing the previous all-time high of $5.816 set in June 2022, months after the Russian invasion of Ukraine that kickstarted a major energy crunch in Europe. Read more: How to save money on gas over Labor Day weekend Diesel is a critical fuel for the global economy, underpinning the world's goods trade — from 18-wheelers driving products across the country to the fleet of cargo vessels that underpin the marine shipping market. The diesel market is now facing two major stressors that are keeping an already crunched market tight. The US conflict in Iran has cut off the flow of refined products from the Persia Gulf, while attacks on oil refineries throughout Russia by the Ukrainian military has shuttered capacity from one of the world's major diesel suppliers. The Middle East and Russia accounted for roughly a third of global diesel exports in 2025. More from Yahoo Scout How do current diesel stockpiles compare to historical levels? What economic impacts could record diesel prices create nationwide? What factors are driving US diesel prices to record highs? Why are global refiners unable to increase production capacity? In the US, stockpiles of distillate fuels such as diesel and gasoline are at their lowest levels on record for this time of year, while on the East Coast — the primary driver of heating demand — stockpiles are at all-time lows. Those shortages have arrived just as the northeast region enters the winter heating season, when demand for fuel typically spikes as consumers turn up their heaters. A drone view shows the BP oil refinery, as nearly 800 workers are locked out of their jobs without pay, in Whiting, Indiana, U.S., July 22, 2026 REUTERS/Eric Cox · Reuters / REUTERS "US diesel prices have never been this high, and now the countdown starts for the trickle down to everything consumers buy," Patrick de Haan, vice president of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy. "Record diesel will start funneling down into the economy." The all-time high for the crucial shipping fuel comes after President Trump called corporate refining leaders to the White House on Tuesday, pressing the executives to raise their production of gasoline and diesel to offset shortages that are driving price pressures as the administration looks ahead to coming midterm elections. However, global refiners are running their systems at near-100% capacity, companies such as US refinery leader Marathon Petroleum ( MPC ) and British oil giant Shell plc ( SHEL ) said in their most recent earnings reports, leaving the refining market with little capacity to ramp up throughput. While oil prices have eased somewhat off their wartime highs set in March, prices are up roughly 5% from their July 18 low. Diesel prices, however, have rushed forward by roughly 40% since the same date. Story Continues "The world is short hydrocarbons, and that is contributing to higher prices for all kinds of goods and services as commodity shocks work their way through supply chains," Rabobank senior market strategist Benjamin Picton wrote to clients on Thursday. articles.title: Teva (TEVA) Backed a Bid of Up to $125M in Cash Plus Assumed Liabilities for BioXcel’s Assets. Is Bankruptcy-Sale Risk Worth the At-Home Opportunity?
articles.content: Teva (TEVA) Backed a Bid of Up to $125M in Cash Plus Assumed Liabilities for BioXcel’s Assets. Is Bankruptcy-Sale Risk Worth the At-Home Opportunity? Jeff Lewis Fri, September 4, 2026 at 12:01 PM EDT 4 min read TEVA BTAI TEVA Teva Pharmaceuticals International GmbH, a subsidiary of Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NYSE: TEVA ), agreed to serve as the stalking-horse bidder for substantially all assets of BioXcel Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:BTAI) and certain affiliates through a court-supervised Chapter 11 auction. Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NYSE:TEVA) is the parent of the bidder and guarantor of the milestone-payment obligations. The proposed consideration consists of $57.5 million in cash at closing and up to $67.5 million of contingent cash consideration, for a maximum of $125 million, plus specified assumed liabilities. The portfolio includes IGALMI, the associated BXCL501 program, and other assets extending beyond IGALMI and neuroscience. The pending supplemental New Drug Application seeks to expand the IGALMI label to include at-home treatment of acute agitation associated with schizophrenia or bipolar I or II disorder in adults. The FDA assigned a November 14, 2026 PDUFA target action date. A competing bidder may still submit a superior offer, and any transaction requires bankruptcy-court approval. Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (TEVA): Among Small-Cap Healthcare Stocks Hedge Funds is Buying Bull Case The purchase agreement creates a qualified form of risk sharing. The $57.5 million closing payment is fixed, while up to $67.5 million depends on contingent outcomes. Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NYSE:TEVA) can therefore pursue the broader outpatient opportunity without paying the maximum cash consideration at closing. IGALMI is already approved for acute agitation associated with schizophrenia or bipolar I or II disorder in adults, but current administration must occur under healthcare-provider supervision. An expanded at-home label could allow treatment earlier in an agitation episode and reduce reliance on emergency departments or other monitored facilities. The commercial fit also appears logical. Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NYSE:TEVA) already markets psychiatric and neurological products, providing relationships with prescribers and payers that could support an outpatient launch. Subject to the purchase agreement and court approval, Section 363 may transfer acquired assets free and clear of certain debts, liens, and interests. Specified assumed liabilities would remain. The breakup fee and expense reimbursement if another bidder prevails also require court approval. Bear Case The stalking-horse position does not guarantee ownership. Another bidder could force Teva Pharmaceuticals International GmbH to increase the offer or abandon the acquisition. The assumption of specified liabilities and inclusion of assets outside neuroscience also mean the maximum cash figure does not capture the entire economic commitment or integration burden. Story Continues The central commercial opportunity remains dependent on the FDA. The safety and effectiveness of IGALMI for at-home use have not been established. The current label warns about hypotension, orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, QT-interval prolongation, and somnolence. Current use requires healthcare-provider supervision, including monitoring of vital signs and alertness. Those warnings become more consequential outside a clinical setting. The FDA could reject the supplemental application or approve a narrower label with patient-selection, caregiver or monitoring requirements. Such restrictions could limit adoption and reduce the value of the contingent-payment structure. Hedge Fund Sentiment The filings available so far reflect positions held before Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NYSE:TEVA) announced the proposed acquisition of BioXcel Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:BTAI) assets. Insider Monkey's database showed 54 hedge funds holding Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NYSE:TEVA) at the end of 2Q2026, up from 52 funds three months earlier. Conclusion The proposed structure shares some regulatory risk through contingent consideration, but it does not remove auction, assumed-liability, or approval risk. The transaction becomes compelling only if Teva Pharmaceuticals International GmbH secures the assets at a disciplined total cost and the FDA grants an at-home label broad enough to support meaningful outpatient adoption. Until then, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (NYSE:TEVA) has a potentially useful strategic opportunity rather than a completed acquisition. While we acknowledge the potential of TEVA as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: Yen's changing fortunes might finally be spooking the bears
articles.content: Yen's changing fortunes might finally be spooking the bears FILE PHOTO: Holograms, which show different images and colours depending on the angle at which they are viewed, are seen on the new Japanese 1,000 yen banknote as the new note is displayed at a currency museum of the Bank of Japan in Tokyo, Japan July 3, 2024. REUTERS/Issei Kato/Pool/File Photo · Reuters By Dhara Ranasinghe, Rae Wee and Atsuko Aoyama Fri, September 4, 2026 at 11:38 AM EDT 5 min read JPY=X By Dhara Ranasinghe, Rae Wee and Atsuko Aoyama LONDON/SINGAPORE/TOKYO, Sept 4 (Reuters) - Six weeks after hitting a four-decade low against the dollar, the tide appears to be turning for the battered yen as a host of factors finally smoke out traders who have spent years betting against the Japanese currency. More from Yahoo Scout What factors are driving the yen's recent recovery? How might Bank of Japan rate hikes affect yen? What role do carry trade unwinds play here? Could Japanese capital repatriation strengthen the yen further? While central bank rate hikes and record currency intervention have failed to provide lasting support for the ‌yen, new tailwinds from capital repatriation, unwinding carry trades and U.S. political pressure are now giving short speculators cause to rethink their long-term game. The yen is on track for a roughly 2% surge against ‌the greenback this week — the most since a rare joint U.S. and Japan intervention at the end of July to lift the yen. "The market psychology around the yen appears to be changing," said Rong Ren Goh, a fixed income portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments. "Investors seem increasingly reluctant to ​aggressively short the JPY (yen), particularly with the prospect of a BOJ rate hike in September adding another layer of risk to the trade." The Bank of Japan is expected to lift its key rate by 25 basis points (bps) this month and markets are also contemplating the possibility of a 50-bps hike or a series of rapid increases in coming months. Nevertheless, a 50-bps September hike is still seen as extremely unlikely, particularly under Governor Kazuo Ueda's cautious leadership. All the same, the shift in mood is backed up by money flows. Data from Citigroup indicate positioning on the yen has flipped from bearish to bullish since the start of August, with interbank flow data showing leveraged funds, banks and real-money investors all net-buying yen this week. The convergence ‌of central bank policy, investment flows and speculative positioning is adding to volatility. The ⁠yen is also up almost 2% against the euro and Australian dollar this week. Stephen Jen, CEO and co-CIO of Eurizon SLJ Asset Management, said the risk of a rapid unwind of yen-based carry trades is rising, in a similar way to 1998 when the collapse of Long-Term Capital Management forced banks and hedge funds to rapidly deleverage. The yen has long ⁠been the favoured currency for the carry trade, where investors borrow cheaply in yen to invest elsewhere. "When a currency is so extremely undervalued, and positioning is so extended, movements like this one will occur increasingly frequently before a big move," Jen said. "It's a bit like earthquakes. The tectonic plates are grating on each other with great forces." Story Continues INTERVENTIONS AND THE FED The yen's years-long weakening trend accelerated this year as fiscal concerns mounted around stimulus plans by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and a strong belief that the BOJ ​was "behind ​the curve" in tightening monetary policy. Tokyo unleashed record solo intervention in April-May when the yen weakened beyond the 160 per dollar line. But ​a key moment came in July-August when Tokyo was joined by Washington in a rare ‌bout of coordinated action after the currency weakened to 163.99, a level not seen since 1986. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has long believed rate hikes were the right medicine for the weak yen, and he pressed the BOJ at a Group of 20 finance chiefs meeting this week. That was followed by a speech by BOJ board member Hajime Takata, the sole dissenter to a July decision to keep rates steady, who raised the spectre of 50-bps moves or hikes in quicker succession. "His (Takata's) remarks about consecutive rate hikes and sharper margins were dramatic," said Yoshio Iguchi, chief strategy officer at Traders Securities. "If this becomes consensus, it could be a game changer for the yen." Odds are now 97% that the BOJ will raise its key rate by 25 bps to 1.25%, according to Tokyo Tanshi data, up from 52% a month ago. The figures show a 27% chance of a rate increase in October and 56% odds in December. Meanwhile, ‌there are signs a sudden lurch higher in Japanese government bond yields to historic levels is compelling domestic institutional investors to repatriate ​money. Global markets shuddered in July when Japan floated the possibility of a pivot by its $1.8 trillion Government Pension Investment Fund back into domestic ​assets. Official data show Japanese investors are shedding foreign bonds at the fastest pace in four years. "The immediate ​story behind the yen's gain is the suggestion that the BOJ could raise more than expected, and that seemed to catch everybody's attention," said Bart Wakabayashi, branch manager at State ‌Street in Tokyo. "But if you take it a step back further, the biggest single factor ​is the possibility that Japanese investors are more inclined to ​invest domestically, including liquidating overseas assets." Real money short underweight positions on the yen are at the highest in five years according to State Street's proprietary data, Wakabayashi said, setting the scene for a potential "reversion" to neutral or overweight levels. The Federal Reserve is another component. Traders trimmed U.S. rate hike bets this month after dovish comments by Fed Governor Christopher Waller, giving the BOJ a chance to narrow a rate gap that ​has been a major factor in yen weakness. The shrinking advantage of overseas rates will ‌also act to unwind yen carry trades. A reversal of short bets could have a dramatic effect. JPMorgan estimates that since Prime Minister Takaichi took office last October, yen shorts have accumulated up to ​around 17 trillion yen ($109 billion). "If this position were to be fully unwound, USD/JPY could fall to the 142–146 range," JPMorgan analysts Junya Tanase and Ikue Saito wrote in a note. articles.title: Algonquin (AQN) is Selling its Chilean Water Stake for $126.5M. Will Simplification Improve Returns?
articles.content: Algonquin (AQN) is Selling its Chilean Water Stake for $126.5M. Will Simplification Improve Returns? Jeff Lewis Fri, September 4, 2026 at 11:32 AM EDT 4 min read AQN AQN Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (NYSE: AQN ) agreed to sell its approximately 64% interest in Chilean water utility Suralis S.A. to a fund managed by Toesca S.A. Administradora General de Fondos. The transaction is expected to generate $126.5 million in proceeds, plus an earnout opportunity of up to $1.5 million. Both amounts are denominated in U.S. dollars. Toesca already owns approximately 30% of Suralis. The agreement advances a strategic reset built around a simpler regulated utility portfolio. Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (NYSE:AQN) expects to use the proceeds for debt reduction and capital recycling into its $3.2 billion regulated capital plan for 2026 through 2028. The transaction is expected to close within the next two quarters, subject to customary conditions, including merger-control approval. The logic is straightforward. Capital tied to a Chilean water business can support core regulated utility infrastructure spending. However, the base proceeds represent just under 4% of the three-year capital plan. The transaction supports the strategy but cannot materially reshape leverage. Why Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (AQN) Crashed On Wednesday Bull Case The strongest argument for the sale is improved focus. Exiting Suralis reduces exposure to a separate regulatory regime and currency while concentrating resources on regulated utility operations closer to the center of the portfolio. A narrower footprint should make capital allocation easier and reduce organizational complexity. Debt paydown also has tangible value. Lower borrowings can reduce interest costs and preserve financing capacity as Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (NYSE:AQN) executes its capital plan. Reinvesting sale proceeds into regulated infrastructure could support rate-base growth and more predictable earnings if approved returns exceed the cost of funding. The transaction also reinforces management's willingness to recycle capital instead of relying entirely on new debt or equity. That discipline matters for a capital-intensive utility. Simplification can improve returns when proceeds from the divested Suralis stake move into projects with better risk-adjusted economics. Bear Case The size of the sale limits the upside. Even if the full earnout is received, maximum consideration would be $128 million, or only 4% of the $3.2 billion plan. Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (NYSE:AQN) will still need substantial internally generated cash and external financing to complete planned investments. The disposal also removes an established regulated water business serving communities in Chile's Los Lagos and Los Rios regions. That means surrendering earnings and geographic diversification. The announcement did not quantify Suralis's earnings contribution or provide a transaction multiple, making it difficult to determine whether the price fully compensates for the income being sold. Story Continues There is also execution risk until closing. Merger-control approval remains outstanding, and the earnout is contingent rather than guaranteed. More importantly, capital recycling creates value only if debt reduction and reinvestment generate returns above the earnings lost from Suralis after taxes and transaction costs. Hedge Fund Sentiment The filings available so far reflect positions held before Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (NYSE:AQN) reported the agreement to sell its Suralis stake. Insider Monkey's database showed 24 hedge funds holding Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (NYSE:AQN) at the end of 2Q2026, down from 28 funds three months earlier. Conclusion The Suralis sale is strategically coherent but financially incremental. Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (NYSE:AQN) can benefit from lower debt, fewer geographic distractions, and greater emphasis on core regulated utilities. Still, a transaction equal to roughly 4% of the capital plan is not large enough to transform leverage or growth. The decisive test will be whether the recycled capital earns attractive regulated returns while balance-sheet metrics improve. For now, simplification supports the recovery thesis, but execution across the broader capital plan will determine whether returns improve sustainably. While we acknowledge the potential of AQN as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: Medicare Advantage Lets You In at 65 With No Questions. Medigap Asks Them Forever After. The Switch Most Retirees Can’t Make at 72.
articles.content: Medicare Advantage Lets You In at 65 With No Questions. Medigap Asks Them Forever After. The Switch Most Retirees Can’t Make at 72. David Beren Fri, September 4, 2026 at 12:19 PM EDT 6 min read Quick Read Medicare Advantage accepts enrollees at 65 without health questions, but Medigap's guaranteed issue window closes after six months and locks out most people permanently. Without Medigap, Original Medicare exposes retirees to a $1,736 Part A deductible and uncapped 20% Part B coinsurance with no annual out-of-pocket limit. Several states including New York, California, and Connecticut offer birthday rules or continuous guaranteed issue rights that let retirees switch without medical underwriting. Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor) Medicare Advantage and Medigap look like two flavors of the same choice at age 65, though they work very differently. Enrollment access is easy at 65 and tightens sharply by 72 for most people who try to switch back. That asymmetry is the entire story, and it shapes a decision that most new retirees treat as reversible when, in most states, it effectively is not. Ihar Halavach / Shutterstock.com The mechanism behind this asymmetry is straightforward. Medicare Advantage plans, the private managed care alternative to Original Medicare, must accept any eligible enrollee during the annual enrollment period and initial eligibility, regardless of health. Medigap, the supplemental insurance that covers Original Medicare's cost sharing, works the opposite way. Federal law guarantees Medigap issue only during a six-month open enrollment window that begins the month a beneficiary is 65 or older and enrolled in Medicare Part B. After that window closes, insurers in most states may medically underwrite, meaning they can ask health questions, charge higher premiums, impose waiting periods for pre-existing conditions, or decline coverage outright. Why the Switch at 72 Usually Fails A common scenario plays out as follows. A healthy 65-year-old picks Medicare Advantage for the low or zero premium and the bundled dental, vision, and drug benefits. Years later, after a cancer diagnosis or a heart procedure, the network feels narrow or the prior authorization rules feel restrictive. She wants to return to Original Medicare and add a Medigap policy. Original Medicare will take her back. The Medigap insurer will run underwriting and, given her chart, may say no. Now you can learn the strategies wealthy retirees use to fund their retirement with The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income from Fisher Investments. Download the guide today! (sponsor) Story Continues The real risk is the financial exposure that follows. Original Medicare has no annual out-of-pocket maximum. In 2026, the Part A inpatient hospital deductible is $1,736 per benefit period, daily hospital coinsurance for days 61 through 90 is $434, and lifetime reserve days cost $868 per day. The Part B standard premium is $202.90 with a $283 annual deductible, and Part B continues to charge 20% coinsurance on covered services with no ceiling. A serious illness without a supplement can compound into tens of thousands of dollars in a single benefit period, and that is before IRMAA surcharges and coverage gaps enter the picture, which we mapped out in a free guide to Medicare's hidden bills. A Social Security check doesn't stretch far enough to cover that. The 2027 cost-of-living adjustment is tracking at 3.1% based on one of three Q3 months of CPI data. Average annual household spending was $78,535 in 2024, according to the Consumer Expenditure Survey, and health care is a rising share of that for older households. State Rules That Change the Math Underwriting restrictions are not universal. Several states require guaranteed issue on a continuing or annual basis, and others have birthday or anniversary rules that allow a switch without underwriting within a set window. New York and Connecticut have continuous guaranteed issue. Massachusetts and Maine have annual or continuous protections of varying scope. California, Oregon, Idaho, Illinois, Nevada, Louisiana, Oklahoma, and a handful of others use birthday rules that open a limited window each year. This is state law, so the neighbor's experience in one state does not predict the outcome in another. Federal law also carves out specific guaranteed issue rights that survive the initial window. A trial right applies when a beneficiary joins Medicare Advantage at first eligibility and switches back to Original Medicare within the first year, generally preserving a right to buy a supplement. Additional guaranteed issue situations include the Medicare Advantage plan leaving the service area, the beneficiary moving out of the plan's network area, and certain involuntary plan terminations. Where Medicare Advantage Still Fits There are some clear benefits to Medicare Advantage. Monthly premiums are often minimal or zero beyond what you already pay for Part B. Plans also include an out-of-pocket maximum, something Original Medicare does not offer, and they usually wrap dental, vision, hearing, and Part D prescription coverage into one package. The downsides are the network restrictions, prior authorization hoops, and referral requirements you have to work through. Medigap works differently. You have to buy a separate Part D drug plan, and you pay a monthly premium that typically increases with age in most states. Switching between Medicare Advantage plans during annual enrollment is usually not a problem. But going in the opposite direction, from Medicare Advantage back to Original Medicare with a Medigap supplement, is where things get difficult. And the difficulty only grows with every new condition that shows up in your medical records. What the Decision at 65 Actually Is The choice at first eligibility is more consequential than it appears because it is effectively one-way in most states. A prospective enrollee should read the initial Medigap open enrollment as a rare and finite right, confirm what the home state's rules allow later, and weigh whether the network of a Medicare Advantage plan will still fit ten or fifteen years out. What matters most is the cost of trying to change course at 72, when the questions on the underwriting form start deciding the answer. articles.title: Larry Fink now calls Bitcoin ‘digital gold’ after once calling it ‘an index of money laundering’
articles.content: Larry Fink now calls Bitcoin ‘digital gold’ after once calling it ‘an index of money laundering’ Sam Bourgi Fri, September 4, 2026 at 11:30 AM EDT 5 min read BTC-USD BLK Bitcoin's rise from an obscure digital asset to the heart of Wall Street has had an unlikely backer: Larry Fink, the BlackRock CEO who eventually came around to Bitcoin's promise — and its enormously lucrative potential. The Observer recently traced Fink's seven-year evolution, from calling Bitcoin "an index of money laundering" in 2017 to recognizing its "digital gold" characteristics years later, just before his firm turned Bitcoin into one of its fastest-growing investment products. Must Read Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028. Here are 4 moves to make before the window closes Of course, Bitcoin has a long history of winning over its critics. Even Michael Saylor, the Bitcoin bull who transformed Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, into the world's largest corporate Bitcoin holder, was once a skeptic. In 2013, Saylor famously declared that Bitcoin's "days are numbered." Today, Strategy holds more than 845,000 BTC on its balance sheet, according to BitcoinTreasuries.NET . For Fink, the epiphany may have been driven partly by Bitcoin's appeal as a "debasement trade" — a scarce asset investors can turn to when they're worried about currencies losing purchasing power. But the business opportunity was impossible to ignore. In January 2024, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) alongside 10 other spot Bitcoin ETFs, giving investors a regulated and familiar way to gain direct exposure to Bitcoin's price without having to buy or custody the cryptocurrency themselves. Then IBIT started breaking records. As CoinDesk reported , the fund reached $70 billion in assets in just 341 trading days, making it BlackRock's biggest fee-generating ETF. When Bitcoin surged above $126,000 last October, IBIT briefly approached $100 billion in assets, reaching that threshold five times faster than any ETF in history, according to Bloomberg. Wall Street access doesn't eliminate Bitcoin risk While IBIT made it easier for investors to gain exposure to Bitcoin — and helped broaden its appeal beyond crypto's traditional base — it didn't insulate them from the asset's notoriously volatile swings. That became painfully clear this year. By June, Bitcoin had fallen below $60,000 , marking a roughly 53% decline from its October peak. Story Continues The selloff also tested investors' appetite for Bitcoin ETFs. U.S. spot Bitcoin funds suffered a record eight consecutive weeks of net outflows between May and early July, shedding roughly $8.3 billion over that stretch, according to SoSoValue data analyzed by The Block . The waters have steadied somewhat since then, with Bitcoin reclaiming $80,000 after a powerful rebound that began in August. The rally gained momentum after the Treasury announced it would at least double buybacks of longer-dated government debt, a move that helped ease pressure on bond yields and boosted risk assets. Around the same time, President Donald Trump hosted crypto and finance executives at the White House, where he urged Congress to pass a "fair version" of the crypto-focused CLARITY Act. But the rebound doesn't erase what came before. ETF investors have learned that wrapping Bitcoin in a familiar Wall Street product doesn't make its sharp swings disappear. BlackRock's answer to that volatility isn't to avoid Bitcoin altogether, but to size the exposure accordingly. Read More: Vanguard reveals what's coming for U.S. stocks — and it could be bad news for this group of investors How much Bitcoin belongs in a portfolio? In 2024, BlackRock suggested that a 1% to 2% Bitcoin allocation could be reasonable for investors who believe the asset will become more widely adopted and are willing to accept the risks that come with its volatility. Its analysis put Bitcoin in roughly the same risk-budgeting range as the "Magnificent Seven" technology stocks in a traditional 60/40 portfolio. Fink has also contemplated what larger institutional allocations could mean for Bitcoin's price. During the 2025 World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, he said he had discussed with a sovereign wealth fund whether it should allocate 2% or 5% of its portfolio to Bitcoin. If allocations of that size became widespread among institutional investors, Fink said Bitcoin could eventually reach as high as $700,000, according to MarketWatch . Others in the industry have made a similar case for modest but concentrated crypto exposure. Vanessa Grellet, managing partner at Arche Capital, told a Grayscale Investments conference earlier this year that a 1% to 5% allocation to Bitcoin or Ether has historically improved risk-adjusted returns in a traditional 60/40 portfolio, aided by crypto's correlation characteristics. "The institutional momentum around digital assets is undeniable," Grellet said , pointing to spot ETF flows, corporate treasury allocations and growing interest from sovereign wealth funds. articles.title: Ballard Power (BLDP) Bought GeoPura at an Enterprise Value of About $400M. Can Recurring Revenue Justify the 14% Pro Forma Stake?
articles.content: Ballard Power (BLDP) Bought GeoPura at an Enterprise Value of About $400M. Can Recurring Revenue Justify the 14% Pro Forma Stake? Jeff Lewis Fri, September 4, 2026 at 11:26 AM EDT 3 min read BLDP BLDP Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ: BLDP ) completed its acquisition of GeoPura Limited on August 28, 2026. The £275 million of upfront consideration comprised £82.5 million in cash, 49.6 million newly issued shares, and restricted share units that will settle into another 1.1 million shares. Former GeoPura Limited shareholders now hold approximately 14.1% of Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) on a pro forma basis. The £301.1 million enterprise value, or about $400 million, includes the assumption of 50% of the debt associated with the HyMarnham joint venture. It excludes up to £27.5 million of contingent consideration. The central question is whether GeoPura Limited's recurring Energy-as-a-Service model can produce enough growth and margin expansion to justify the valuation and new shareholders' stake. Is Ballard Power Systems Inc. (BLDP) the Best Hydrogen Stock to Buy According to Billionaires? Bull Case GeoPura Limited develops, leases, and sells Hydrogen Power Units while producing and delivering the hydrogen that runs them. Combining those capabilities with the fuel-cell technology of Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) creates an end-to-end offering spanning hydrogen production, logistics, refueling, fuel cells and stationary power generation. In addition to component sales, Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) can earn recurring leasing and hydrogen-supply revenue. GeoPura Limited also brings customer relationships across construction, data centers, media, infrastructure and government, giving the combined business direct access to large power users. Revenue visibility is another attraction. GeoPura Limited owns 50% of HyMarnham Power, which secured a UK government agreement providing 15 years of hydrogen-production revenue support. Management identified approximately $25 million of annual run-rate EBITDA synergies from revenue expansion and cost optimization. EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, is a non-GAAP measure. Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) ended the second quarter with $502.1 million of cash and cash equivalents, before paying the acquisition's £82.5 million cash component. Bear Case The valuation sets a demanding hurdle. The £301.1 million enterprise value is approximately 7.9 times GeoPura Limited's projected 2026 revenue of £38 million, before any contingent payment. A revenue shortfall would push the multiple higher. Recurring revenue does not automatically produce attractive returns. Hydrogen production, storage and distribution remain capital-intensive, while utilization, electricity costs and policy support affect project economics. Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) must integrate fuel-cell engineering, power-unit manufacturing, hydrogen production and fleet logistics while controlling cash consumption. Story Continues The transaction gives former GeoPura Limited shareholders 14.1% of the post-closing equity before the synergy benefits have been demonstrated. Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) also reported a company-defined adjusted EBITDA loss of $9.8 million in the second quarter, compared with a $30.6 million loss a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA starts with EBITDA and adjusts for stock-based compensation, transaction gains and losses, finance and other income, impairment charges, and unrealized foreign-exchange gains and losses. Hedge Fund Sentiment The filings available so far reflect positions held before Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) reported the closing of the GeoPura Limited acquisition. Insider Monkey's database showed 22 hedge funds holding Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) at the end of 2Q2026, up from 13 funds three months earlier. Conclusion GeoPura Limited gives Ballard Power Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:BLDP) recurring service revenue, hydrogen logistics and direct customer relationships. Investors now need evidence of strong Hydrogen Power Unit utilization, attractive recurring gross margins, and conversion of the $25 million synergy target into cash earnings. Until those measures emerge, the acquisition offers a credible strategic path, but its price and ownership transfer leave the proof burden on execution. While we acknowledge the potential of BLDP as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: PG&E launches strategic review of energy business and financing
articles.content: PG&E launches strategic review of energy business and financing PG&E said the review will include consultations with regulators · Power Technology Shree Mishra Thu, September 3, 2026 at 4:19 AM CDT 2 min read PCG US-based electric utility PG&E and its subsidiary the Pacific Gas and Electric Company have announced a strategic review of the organisation's energy business structure and financing, alongside plans to defer approximately $2bn in planned investment in 2027. The company stated that the moves are intended to help maintain essential safety investments and compliance standards while reducing near-term borrowing costs for California customers. A newly formed Strategic Review Committee made up of four independent directors from PG&E's board will lead the review. The committee will evaluate regulatory, financial, operational and strategic alternatives to determine the best organisation and financing structure for the company. PG&E said the review will include consultations with regulators, policymakers and stakeholders in California and focus on achieving a financially sound, investment-grade status. The objectives outlined for the review include upholding safety performance, improving customer affordability, strengthening system reliability and resiliency, and maintaining commitments to labour agreements, pensions and claims. As an initial step in this process, PG&E plans to revise its 2027 capital plan by deferring roughly $2bn in planned spending while continuing with around $11.4bn in investments that year. According to the company, the adjustment would reduce its debt financing needs by $2bn, which is expected to result in lower financing costs for customers. The company identified specific projects and programmes that can be postponed or delayed to slow capital expenditure growth. However, it emphasised that funding for critical safety initiatives and compliance requirements, including those related to its Wildfire Mitigation Plan and safety certification standards, will continue unchanged. PG&E said it would provide further updates on the progress of the strategic review during its regular quarterly earnings calls or in the event of significant developments. PG&E CEO Patti Poppe said: "Over the last several years, PG&E has made meaningful progress improving safety, reliability and affordability for our customers. "But California's wildfire liability framework continues to create financing risks that drive higher costs, affect customer affordability and limit investment in the energy system. Something has to change so that we can better serve our customers. That is why we are taking action today." articles.title: Box (BOX) Turns Enterprise Files Into AI Fuel
articles.content: Box (BOX) Turns Enterprise Files Into AI Fuel Maham Fatima Thu, September 3, 2026 at 4:10 AM CDT 4 min read BOX DATB.PVT On August 25, Box Inc. (NYSE: BOX ) reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 results that beat management's own guidance across the board, with revenue climbing 9% to $321.1 million as customers piled into the company's priciest tier, Enterprise Advanced. The bigger story sits underneath the headline number. Box is repositioning itself as the security layer that lets AI agents from Anthropic, Databricks, and Slack actually touch a company's files, and that shift is starting to show up in the billings line. Box (BOX) Turns Enterprise Files Into AI Fuel The Enterprise Advanced Payoff Billings jumped 17% to $309.5 million, a figure management tied directly to booking strength and record second-quarter wins, which suggests customers are signing bigger contracts rather than trickling in seat by seat. Net retention rose to 106%, ahead of the 105% the company had guided to, driven by both seat expansion and higher price per seat. That combination matters because it means existing customers are both growing their headcount on the platform and paying more per person, a dual engine that is harder to replicate than growth from new logos alone. Suites, Box's bundled higher-tier offering, now make up 69% of revenue, up from 63% a year earlier, and customers paying at least $100,000 annually grew 10% year over year. A major federal agency illustrated the pattern in the flesh, upgrading to Enterprise Advanced with a fourfold seat expansion to replace several separate software vendors it had been using for contract management and research. Operating margin expanded to 29.4%, and free cash flow jumped 67% to $59.7 million, evidence that the growth is not being bought with discounts. Box also introduced new Model Context Protocol integrations with partners including Anthropic, Databricks, and Slack, letting AI agents execute multistep tasks directly inside a customer's Box environment rather than just answering questions about files stored there. Cracks Beneath The Guidance Not everything in the quarter was clean. CFO Dylan Smith flagged that gross margin faces a constraint tied to "limited access to certain components of the infrastructure," language that points to capacity limits at the cloud providers Box relies on to run its AI features, and management guided third-quarter gross margin down to roughly 80.5% from the 81.2% just posted. Operating margin guidance for the third quarter also steps down to about 28%, a full percentage point below the 29.4% Box just delivered, even as the top line keeps growing. Currency is another drag that will not disappear on its own. The company absorbed a $0.04 per share hit from foreign exchange in the quarter and expects roughly $0.09 off full-year earnings per share, which is baked into the raised full-year EPS guidance of $1.54. And while 9% reported revenue growth beat expectations, it is still a business growing in the high single digits, a pace that leaves little room for stumbles if Enterprise Advanced adoption cools or larger AI platforms decide to build competing file-governance tools of their own rather than partner with Box. Story Continues Wall Street's Mixed Read Hedge fund ownership ticked up to 37 funds from 36 the prior quarter, a modest gain that reads more like steady interest than a rush of new conviction. Short interest sits at 14.08% of the float, a level that signals a real bear camp is positioned against the stock rather than routine hedging. As of September 2, the forward P/E of 18.90 is not an expensive multiple for a company posting double-digit constant currency growth and expanding margins, which is part of what makes the heavy short interest notable. That combination suggests that the market is unsettled about whether Box's AI pivot converts into durable growth or gets squeezed by the same infrastructure constraints management just flagged. What Comes Next Box's quarter makes a clear case that Enterprise Advanced and its AI integrations are pulling in bigger contracts and stickier customers, and the margin and free cash flow numbers back that up. But the same call that delivered the beat also introduced a gross margin headwind from infrastructure capacity and a step down in near-term operating margin guidance, so the profitability story is not as clean going forward as the quarter just reported. For the bulls, the test is whether Enterprise Advanced adoption keeps accelerating billings and suites mix through the back half of the year. While we acknowledge the potential of BOX as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: HEICO Corp. (HEI): Record Profits And Bold Bets Power Aerospace Supplier’s Surge
articles.content: HEICO Corp. (HEI): Record Profits And Bold Bets Power Aerospace Supplier’s Surge Maham Fatima Thu, September 3, 2026 at 4:17 AM CDT 4 min read HEI On August 26, HEICO Corporation (NYSE: HEI ) delivered a third quarter that management itself struggled to summarize without repeating the word record. Net income jumped 33% to $235.4 million, net sales climbed 23% to $1.4 billion, and the company generated $345.3 million in cash from operations, a figure equal to nearly 150% of net income. For a business that has now compounded earnings for close to four decades, the bigger question is not whether HEICO can grow, but how long it can keep growing this fast. HEICO Corp. (HEI): Record Profits And Bold Bets Power Aerospace Supplier's Surge Margins Widen As Orders Pile Up The headline number is 14% organic growth across the company, but the more telling detail is where that growth showed up. The Electronic Technologies Group posted an all-time quarterly record, with net sales up 36% to $483.5 million and operating income up 55% to $125.6 million, as its operating margin expanded from 22.8% to 26%. The Flight Support Group grew net sales 18% to $947.8 million while its operating income rose 24%, outpacing revenue growth as the segment shifted toward higher-value products rather than volume alone. Co-CEO Victor Mendelson said some missile defense customers have asked for production increases as high as tenfold on specific programs, while industrial technology tied to AI and data center buildouts is now feeding demand inside the electronics segment too. Management also pointed to the integration of Wencor, with Eric Mendelson calling the combination "an absolute home run for HEICO as well as for Wencor." On the balance sheet, HEICO issued $1.2 billion in senior unsecured notes to pay down its revolver and extended that facility's maturity to June 2031, with room to grow capacity to $3 billion. Net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.57 times. The company also raised its semiannual dividend 8% to $0.13 per share, its 96th consecutive payout since 1979, and closed acquisitions of Cook Defence Systems and CalRamic Technologies during the quarter. Costs Creep In From All Sides The same demand surge fueling HEICO's growth is straining its supply chain from the other direction. Victor Mendelson warned that lead times for certain raw materials and subcomponents are stretching out and getting more expensive, driven in part by competing demand from the AI and data center markets. Eric Mendelson pointed to a narrower but familiar bottleneck in component repair, noting that a job with 99 parts finished still cannot ship while the company waits on the hundredth. Neither issue derailed this quarter's results, but both suggest the growth machine runs on inputs HEICO does not fully control. Story Continues There is also a one-time cash headwind coming. CFO Carlos Macau flagged a payment to the estate of the company's past chairman and CEO that he said would create a $70 million to $75 million drag on operating cash flow in the fourth quarter, a reminder that even a quarter this strong carries items that will not repeat. Wall Street Still Weighing The Premium Hedge fund ownership of HEICO slipped from 74 funds in the prior quarter to 72 in the most recent one, a modest pullback rather than a retreat. Short interest sits at just 1.44% of float, which suggests little organized skepticism toward the stock despite its size and run. The stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 44.64 as of September 2, a multiple that prices in continued double-digit growth rather than a steady industrial compounder. That combination points to a market that is not betting against HEICO so much as it is betting the growth has to keep showing up to justify the price. What Happens Next Matters Most HEICO's third quarter left little room to argue with the results themselves: record income, record cash flow, and margin expansion in both operating segments. The tension sits in what comes after. For the bulls, the case rests on demand across aerospace, defense, and now AI-adjacent electronics continuing to outrun the company's ability to source parts and materials. While we acknowledge the potential of HEI as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk.
